description: Start a supervised background job or persistent service using run_command's native sandbox and approval rules. Poll or cancel the handle. Final delivery requires every handle to be terminal.

propertyDescriptions.executionScope: Default workspace sandbox. Request host only for an explicit per-command host escalation approved with this invocation. Benchmark remains container-confined.
propertyDescriptions.requiredCapabilities: Compatibility requirements only, never permission grants. test/verify assumes loopback_tcp for runtime IPC. Set [] for checks known not to need IPC. Verify actual cross-command localhost reachability with a bounded probe; do not infer network isolation from a stopped service. Missing capabilities require explicit approval for host execution; Benchmark never escapes.
propertyDescriptions.program: Executable name, path relative to cwd, or absolute local executable. Same resolution and isolation as run_command.
propertyDescriptions.args: Literal structured argv, including multiline code. For cmd /c the complete command must be one argument; no automatic shell-string joining.
propertyDescriptions.cwd: Normal CLI workspace: /workspace or a relative path; other Linux container directories are allowed. Host scope/Full access uses host paths. Benchmark keeps its offline worker paths.
propertyDescriptions.intent: Declared command purpose, not permission. Use test, build or verify for validation.
propertyDescriptions.verificationKind: Optional validation category. Missing verify/test categories default to custom; build defaults to build. Inapplicable or invalid metadata is normalized without blocking execution.
propertyDescriptions.timeoutMs: An optional hard process-lifetime limit. When omitted, the independent background lifetime limit applies instead of run_command's foreground timeout. Runtime returns the effective capped budget across later polls.
propertyDescriptions.backgroundKind: Optional job (default) or service. Job keeps exclusive workspace mutation ownership until it finishes. Service reserves the workspace for the same agent but permits that agent's later tools while the service runs; other agents wait. Declare service only for a process intentionally kept alive during dependent work.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A concise explanation of why this command is needed for the current task.

guidance: Use backgroundKind=service for a dev/API server that must stay alive while this agent runs dependent tools; leave the default job for builds, tests, installs and other finite background work. A running handle confirms process startup, not application readiness. Probe the known local TCP or HTTP endpoint with bounded retries before dependent smoke tests; on Windows, live service stdout may be unavailable until completion. If the probe fails, distinguish an exited process, an unready process and an unreachable port before diagnosing sandbox isolation. Prefer direct test output over a filtering pipeline; Runtime returns execution status separately from validation passed/failed/unknown. Use poll_command for bounded waits and cancel_command when no longer needed. Stop a service when dependent work is done and observe every handle's terminal result. Missing validation metadata is normalized once and remains attached across polls.
